title: What bear markets actually reveal
tweets:
A bear market isn't a verdict on Bitcoin.

It's a stress test — not of the protocol, but of everyone who holds an opinion about it.

What you see in the price chart matters less than what you see in the people watching it. 🧵

When the price is down 70%, a certain type of person appears.

They write the obituaries. They say "I told you so." They explain, with sudden confidence, exactly why this was always a scam.

Most of them couldn't have explained what a block was when the price was at $100k.

When the price hits a new all-time high, a different type of person appears.

They buy because their coworker told them to. They set price targets. They feel clever.

They're not engaging with Bitcoin. They're engaging with a number going up.

Both groups are responding to price, not principle.

The bear market didn't make Bitcoin worth less. It made the noise quieter.

The people who leave in a bear market are the ones who were never really there.

Holding through a bear market isn't stubbornness. It's a statement.

It means you evaluated Bitcoin on its properties — not its price. And your evaluation didn't change just because the crowd's did.

Conviction built on understanding doesn't move with sentiment.

The market is a mirror.

Not for Bitcoin's value — but for your own relationship with uncertainty, pressure, and what you actually believe when the consensus turns against you.

Bear markets don't destroy value. They reveal character.
